literal: Destruction without excellent-wealth learning to-a-person; wealth are-not other those.
translation: Learning is the only imperishable, supreme wealth for a person. All other possessions are not true wealth.
modern: ஒருவருக்கு அழிவில்லாத சிறந்த செல்வம் கல்வியே ஆகும். மற்றவை எல்லாம் உண்மையான செல்வம் ஆகா.
explanation: This couplet declares learning as the ultimate form of wealth. The phrase 'kēṭu il' means without destruction, showing that unlike material riches, education cannot be stolen, diminished, or lost. The word 'māṭu' originally referred to cattle, the ancient measure of riches, and here signifies true wealth. The poet emphasizes that for any person, learning is the supreme wealth, and all other possessions are not wealth at all.
